summary: The 100MHz RF Transceiver has been successfully designed and verified. The system includes an LNA, PA, Gilbert Cell Mixer (used for both RX downconversion and TX upconversion), and a cross-coupled LC LO. The blocks were integrated into RX and TX top levels, and finally into a combined TRX top level. Simulation evidence confirms that the RX path successfully downconverts a 100MHz RF signal to a 10MHz IF signal with >100mVpp amplitude, and the TX path successfully upconverts a 10MHz IF signal to a 100MHz RF signal with >1Vpp amplitude.
evidence:
TRX Top Simulation Results:
- RX_RF_IN: 100 MHz, 20 mVpp input.
- RX_IF_P / RX_IF_N: 10 MHz dominant peak (103 mV amplitude -> 206 mVpp), which is > 100 mVpp. DC level is ~1.3V.
- TX_IF_P / TX_IF_N: 10 MHz, 200 mVpp input.
- TX_RF_OUT: 100 MHz dominant peak (589 mV amplitude -> 1.18 Vpp), which is > 1 Vpp. Total Vpp is 2.15 V. DC level is ~0V (AC coupled).
- LO_P / LO_N: 90 MHz dominant peak (984 mV amplitude -> 1.97 Vpp), which is > 1 Vpp. DC level is ~2.2V.

All individual blocks (LO, LNA, Mixer, PA) and top levels (RX, TX, TRX) have been successfully designed, netlisted, and verified to meet the expected values.
